runs.content: Lithia Motors (LAD) picked up at the previous close ($375.78) — a still-early 3-month momentum setup (+29.0%, RSI 58.8) reinforced by a Q2 EPS beat and a cheap ~12.5x P/E, chosen as market leadership broadens away from the narrow AI-megacap trade (Dow record close vs. Nasdaq −0.8% on weak AI names). FICO was stopped out today at $1,031.89 (−15.93%, −$159.25) after a Wolfe Research downgrade on VantageScore competitive-pressure concerns breached the −15% stop. RIVN (−10.48%) and JBHT (−10.44%) both crossed the −10% signal-assessment threshold but were held — neither carries a Burry conflict. Portfolio net P&L: +$1,154 (+2.40% on $48,000).

ConocoPhillips (COP) picked up at the previous close ($115.04) — Energy was today's leading sector as Brent/WTI spiked on fresh Iran Strait-of-Hormuz shipping restrictions, reinforced by a same-day Q2 earnings beat (EPS $3.24 vs. $2.88 est.) and $3.0B returned to shareholders. No exits today despite a softer broad tape (Dow −0.9%, S&P −0.2%): no position breached the −15% stop, hit a new T1/T2, or tripped the Burry signal-exit rule; FICO rallied to −11.06% (still WATCH, well off stop) while RIVN (−9.43%) and JBHT (−8.63%) drifted further into WATCH, none with a Burry conflict. A stale NVO price from yesterday was corrected to its verified $44.53 close. Portfolio net P&L: +$1,248 (+2.66% on $47,000).
